parsedVerdict.reasoning: This file is declared as domain through the **/*.entity.ts pattern, but its only job is persistence mapping. EmailTemplateEntity is a TypeORM schema definition. @Entity({ name: 'email_templates' }) binds it to a database table, the @Column() decorators map its fields to columns, and @Index({ unique: true }) on title defines a database uniqueness constraint. Table names, column mappings and indexes are persistence concerns, which belong to the infrastructure layer. The class has no domain behaviour or invariants of its own, so it is really an ORM data model. The rubric names persistence logic in a domain file as a failure. Confidence is moderate because the project puts *.entity.ts in the domain layer on purpose, which is a common NestJS/TypeORM convention. Still, judged against the layer's role, persistence mapping is not a domain responsibility.
